# The journalists Bangladesh lost, and the justice that rarely came

> The 62 journalists and media workers killed in Bangladesh since 1972, and where each case stands. A court has convicted someone in only 14 cases.

The Daily Star, 4 November 2026. By Mir Rownak (research, data and visualisation).
Page: https://campaign.thedailystar.net/journalist-killed-1972-2026/

## Summary

Lutfuzzaman Fakir Alif was the most recent. The Netrokona correspondent of Ruposhi Bangla, an internet TV channel, was shot outside a shop in Telunjia village in Durgapur upazila on the evening of 15 October 2026 ([bdnews24](https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/g27omrulpu)). His wife filed a murder case the next day against unidentified people, and police have since arrested two people, [The Daily Star Bangla reported](https://bangla.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/crime-justice/news-3973001). The same report said a Facebook page he ran had published reports on border smuggling. Police have not said why he was killed.

He is the latest name on a list The Daily Star has compiled from the records of the Committee to Protect Journalists, Reporters Without Borders, the International Federation of Journalists, UNESCO, Bangladeshi rights groups and newspaper archives: journalists and media workers killed by violence in Bangladesh since 1972.

Most of them were little known outside their districts. They were upazila correspondents, crime reporters and editors of small dailies, and many had reported on smuggling, drug gangs, armed groups or local politics before they were killed. The Committee to Protect Journalists, which applies a strict test, counts 28 of these deaths as confirmed work-related killings: killed in reprisal for their work, in crossfire or on a dangerous assignment ([CPJ](https://cpj.org/data/killed/asia/bangladesh)). The others are cases in which CPJ has not confirmed a motive, cases it does not list, or killings from before its records begin in 1992. Each record below says which, and what police have said.

What most cases share is what happened next. The trial over the 1998 bomb killing of Saiful Alam Mukul, editor of the Daily Runner in Jashore, has been stalled for years by a High Court application from one of the accused, the public prosecutor told [Views Bangladesh](https://viewsbangladesh.com/journo-mukul-murder-26-years-of-justice-denied). The court deadline for the investigation report into the 2012 killing of Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi has been deferred more than 120 times ([The New Nation](https://dailynewnation.com/news/823172)). In 2021 The Daily Star found that [justice in journalist killings had become "a mirage"](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/journo-killings-justice-mirage-impunity-prevails-2211586).

## The numbers

- 62 journalists and media workers killed in Bangladesh since 1972 are on this list.
- 14 of those cases have ended with a court convicting someone.
- 48 have not. Some are still under investigation or in court, some were closed, and in others no one was ever charged.

## On the page

- [Where they were killed](https://campaign.thedailystar.net/journalist-killed-1972-2026/#h-map): Each dot is one person, placed in the upazila where they were killed.
- [Nearly 13 years to a verdict](https://campaign.thedailystar.net/journalist-killed-1972-2026/#h-bridge): When a verdict does come, it comes slowly.
- [Every name, every case](https://campaign.thedailystar.net/journalist-killed-1972-2026/#list): Newest first. Each record gives what happened, who has been charged and where the case stood at the last report we could find.

## How we counted

- Who is included: journalists and media workers (reporters, correspondents, editors, publishers, photojournalists, online journalists, and bloggers where CPJ counts them as journalists) killed by violence in Bangladesh from 1 January 1972 to 1 November 2026. Accidents and illness are excluded. Inclusion does not mean the killing was linked to the person's journalism; each record says what is known about the motive.
- A case is listed when at least two independent reliable sources, or one strong source (CPJ, RSF, IFJ, UNESCO or a major Bangladeshi daily), confirm the killing. Deaths that remain disputed (bodies found, deaths called suicide or accident) and names that appear in a single list are not included, so the true number is likely higher.
- Records before 1992, when CPJ's database begins, are thin.
- Sheikh Fazlul Haque Moni, editor of Banglar Bani, is included because he was an editor; he was killed in the coup of 15 August 1975, and no source links his killing to his journalism. Convictions in the Bangabandhu murder case are not counted as a conviction in his case, in which all accused were acquitted in 2002.
- Rana Pratap Bairagi, acting editor of Dainik BD Khobor, is included as a journalist killed in 2026. Police say his killing arose from a conflict between banned extremist groups, and the interim government has said it was not linked to journalism.
- "Convicted" means a trial court found at least one person guilty, even if an appeal is pending. In Humayun Kabir Balu's case, the convictions came in a separate explosives case over the same attack; the murder case ended in acquittal.
- Case status is as of the most recent report we found, given in each record. Locations are placed at the centre of the upazila.

## Sources

Sources: CPJ, RSF, IFJ, UNESCO, IFEX, ARTICLE 19, IPI, ASK, PEC, BCDJC, Front Line Defenders, INSI.
